newsitem.title: USA: USDA proposes Dayton, Ohio, as horse entry port.
newsitem.headline: USDA proposes Dayton, Ohio, as horse entry port.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department said Wednesday it was proposing Dayton, Ohio, as an approved port of entry for horses and horse products.
The Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service said it viewed the proposal as noncontroversial. It estimated fewer than 20 horses a year would enter through Dayton.

APHIS said Dayton met the requirements to be a limited port of entry, meaning it had inspection capabilities for animals and products that do not appear to require restraint and holding facilities for inspection.
Comments on the proposal will be accepted through June 23.
